evidence.excerpt: Some manufacturers maintain finished-goods buffers for standard items while also accepting custom orders on a make-to-order basis, creating a hybrid production environment where buffer-stock and pricing policies interact. This paper formulates a Markov decision process for a firm choosing both the reorder point of its standard item and the price it quotes for custom orders, given machine capacity shared between both streams. The state space is characterised by buffer inventory level and current custom-order queue length. Value iteration is used to solve instances with up to 40 inventory levels and 20 queue states. Results show that ignoring the interaction between buffer policy and custom-order pricing leads to a 9% average profit loss. The optimal policy exhibits intuitive threshold structure: custom-order prices rise as both buffer stock falls and custom-order queue grows. A sensitivity study over breakdown rates and demand variability parameters is included.
